title: Participant API process still holds the ground-truth database credential and exposes admin/GT routes

original_titles.title: Single participant-facing API process holds the ground-truth DB credential
Participant-facing API process holds gt_admin credentials and serves gt endpoints
Participant and admin API merged into one process/port/DB role; no separate worker_evaluator/scheduler/runner_gateway roles
Ground-truth schema read/written directly from the API process (admin router uses gt_session)
DB role model deviates: no admin_api or read-only evaluator; gt_admin over-privileged
gt_admin granted write on gt and ALL on app schema (exceeds evaluator need)
Admin and reviewer screens ship in the participant bundle
Participant bundle ships admin/review consoles; no app split and no CI leak grep
Participant SPA bundle statically includes admin and reviewer screens
One SPA/origin serves both the participant and the admin console
Admin API served from the same host/app as the participant API (audience-only separation)
Admin API on same host/audience; step-up is password re-entry; no idempotency keys on admin mutations

problem: main.py includes participant, review and admin routers in one FastAPI process. db.py constructs gt_engine at import time; admin.py imports gt_session and writes to gt.gt_* using the same process. SQL role separation limits what app_api can query, but compromise of any route/process can potentially use the GT credential already available to that process. The frontend also statically imports review/admin modules into one SPA bundle.
impact: A participant endpoint compromise has a path to the process environment and the GT database credential; the answer-key trust boundary is therefore process-level, not just SQL-role-level. Admin route names and console code are also shipped to participants, although server authorization remains authoritative.

evidence_paths: backend/app/routers/admin.py: gt_session imports and GT writes
frontend/src/App.tsx: static imports for review/admin pages
verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Create a participant API app that does not import admin.py, admin_levels.py, db.gt_engine or any module that can load DATABASE_URL_GT. Fail startup if DATABASE_URL_GT is present in the participant process environment.
Create a separate admin/authoring API service behind a separate hostname and identity proxy. It owns staff/admin routes and a narrowly scoped authoring credential.
Move evaluator GT reads into a worker process with a read-only GT DB role. Move GT writes into a distinct authoring service/role; do not grant the evaluator role write access to the GT schema.
Revoke broad grants from gt_admin on app schema; grant only required SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE operations and sequences. Add migration tests that inspect actual grants.

Build separate participant and admin/reviewer frontend entry points or lazy-load role bundles with CI artifact scanning. Confirm the participant artifact contains no admin route/component chunks or GT-authoring strings.

acceptance_criteria: Participant API process has no GT URL, pool, router import or network route.
A runtime compromise test from participant API cannot connect to gt schema.
GT authoring and evaluator roles are least privilege and covered by real PostgreSQL tests.
Participant build artifact excludes admin/reviewer route modules.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

dependencies: Cloudflare Access or equivalent admin identity proxy
